title: Fraction-algebra charts and overlaps of a binomial blowup
statement:
Let $R$ be a domain, $0\ne a\in R$ and $n\ge2$. Put $A=R[x,y]/(xy-a^n)$ and $I=(x,a,y)$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Regard $A$ and its fraction subalgebras inside $\operatorname{Frac}(R)(x)$ via $y=a^n/x$. The standard charts of $\operatorname{Bl}_I\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-nagata-affine-blowup, def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring] have the following isomorphisms, with the displayed forward maps injective into that field:
$$R[x,t]/(xt-a)\xrightarrow{\sim}A[I/x],\quad t\mapsto a/x,\quad y=x^{n-1}t^n,\quad y/x=x^{n-2}t^n;$$
$$R[r,s]/(rs-a^{n-2})\xrightarrow{\sim}A[I/a],\quad r\mapsto x/a,\quad s\mapsto y/a;$$
$$R[y,h]/(yh-a)\xrightarrow{\sim}A[I/y],\quad h\mapsto a/y,\quad x=y^{n-1}h^n,\quad x/y=y^{n-2}h^n.$$
These charts form a cover. Writing $T$ for the Rees degree variable, for $b,c\in\{x,a,y\}$ their overlap $D_+(bT)\cap D_+(cT)$ is $D(c/b)$ in $\operatorname{Spec}A[I/b]$ [def-nagata-affine-proj, def-nagata-homogeneous-away-to-chart]. On the first--middle overlap $D(t)=D(r)$ the transition is
$$r=t^{-1},\quad s=x^{n-2}t^{n-1},\quad x=ar;$$
on the third--middle overlap $D(h)=D(s)$ it is
$$s=h^{-1},\quad r=y^{n-2}h^{n-1},\quad y=as.$$
The first--third overlap is $D(x^{n-2}t^n)$ in the first chart, with $y=x^{n-1}t^n$ and $h=a/y$, and the symmetric description holds in the third chart. The extended ideal $I$ is respectively $(x)$, $(a)$ and $(y)$ on these charts [def-nagata-extended-ideal]. Consequently the closed subscheme $V(I\mathcal O)$ cut out by the extended ideal has affine coordinate rings $\overline R[t]$, $\overline R[r,s]/(rs-\epsilon)$ and $\overline R[h]$, where $\overline R=R/(a)$ and $\epsilon=1$ for $n=2$ and $0$ for $n>2$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal]. For $n=2$ its middle chart is exactly the common overlap of the two outer charts with $h=t^{-1}$; for $n>2$ its two outer charts have empty overlap, and their overlaps with the middle chart lie respectively on $s=0$ and $r=0$.

proof.text: Put $K=\operatorname{Frac}R$, $F=K(x)$, $C_x=R[x,t]/(xt-a)$, $C_a=R[r,s]/(rs-a^{n-2})$ and $C_y=R[y,h]/(yh-a)$. Apply [lem-sfb-binomial-laurent-normal-form] to the nonzero parameters $a^n,a,a^{n-2},a$ (for $n=2$, the third parameter is $1$). It embeds $A$ in $F$ by $y=a^n/x$ and embeds $C_x$ by $t=a/x$. For $C_a$ first use its injective map to $K(U)$, $r=U,s=a^{n-2}/U$, and substitute $U=x/a$; the inverse substitution is $x=aU$, so this is an isomorphism of rational function fields and $s=a^{n-1}/x=y/a$. For $C_y$ use $K(V)$ with $y=V,h=a/V$ and substitute $V=a^n/x$, whose inverse is $x=a^n/V$. All substitutions are defined since $a\ne0$ in the domain $R$. These give exactly the four embeddings in the statement, without asserting any normality of $R$.

source.place: Tag 0804 (lemma-blowing-up-affine), with the existing binomial normal-form lemma for injectivity; agent calculation

proof.text: By [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring], $A[I/x]$ is generated over $A$ by $a/x$ and $y/x$: if $z=ux+va+wy\in I$, then $z/x=u+v(a/x)+w(y/x)$. In $F$, put $t=a/x$. The identities $xt=a$, $y=x^{n-1}t^n$ and $y/x=x^{n-2}t^n$ show that this chart is exactly the image $R[x,t]$ of the injective map from $C_x$. The map is therefore an isomorphism onto the chart. Similarly $A[I/a]$ is generated by $r=x/a,s=y/a$ over $A$, and $x=ar,y=as$ show it is exactly the image $R[r,s]$ of $C_a$; its relation is $rs=xy/a^2=a^{n-2}$. Exchanging $x,y$ gives $A[I/y]=R[y,h]$ with $h=a/y$, $yh=a$, $x=y^{n-1}h^n$ and $x/y=y^{n-2}h^n$. These computations identify the actual fraction subalgebras, hence introduce no extra component or power-torsion quotient.

proof.text: Apply [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart] to each $b\in\{x,a,y\}\subset I$: by [def-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-map] its isomorphism is the one induced by $\theta_b$ onto $D_+(bT)$. By [def-nagata-homogeneous-away-to-chart] it sends a homogeneous fraction $zT^m/(bT)^m$ to $z/b^m$. Thus the fraction-algebra identifications of step 2 are the standard charts with the asserted maps to $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Since $I=(x,a,y)$, [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover] proves that these three opens cover the blowup.

source.place: Tag 0804 (lemma-blowing-up-affine), affine chart identification and finite generator cover

proof.text: For $b,c\in\{x,a,y\}$ apply [lem-weil-pbc-proj-basic-open-intersection] with the degree-one homogeneous elements $f=bT,g=cT$ of the Rees algebra. Both degrees are positive and equal to $1$, so the intersection in the $b$-chart is $D((cT)/(bT))$. The formula in [def-nagata-homogeneous-away-to-chart] identifies this element with $c/b$. This proves the asserted overlap formula for every pair, including repeated indices.

On the first--middle overlap the inverted elements are $t=a/x$ and $r=x/a$, so $r=t^{-1}$. Substitution gives $s=y/a=x^{n-2}t^{n-1}$ and $x=ar$. Conversely the substitution $x=ar,t=r^{-1}$ into the first equation gives $xt=a$, and into $x^{n-2}t^{n-1}$ gives $a^{n-2}/r=s$ by $rs=a^{n-2}$. Thus these are inverse homomorphisms of the localized chart rings, by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-universal-property]. Exchanging $x,t,r$ with $y,h,s$ gives the other transition: $s=h^{-1}$, $r=y^{n-2}h^{n-1}$, $y=as$, with inverse $y=as,h=s^{-1}$. No cancellation by $a$ in an exceptional-fibre ring is used.

source.place: Tag 01M4 (lemma-standard-open), overlap restrictions; agent explicit substitutions

proof.text: For the outer--outer overlap, step 4 inverts $q=y/x=x^{n-2}t^n$ in the first chart. There $y=xq=x^{n-1}t^n$ and $h=t/q$, so $yh=xt=a$ and $h=a/y$ in $F$. In the third chart the inverted element is $q'=x/y=y^{n-2}h^n$, and the inverse formulas are $x=yq'$ and $t=h/q'$. Under the first substitution $q'$ becomes $q^{-1}$: indeed $y^{n-2}(t/q)^n=x^{n-2}t^n/q^2=q^{-1}$. The composites give $x\mapsto xq q^{-1}=x$ and $t\mapsto(t/q)/(q^{-1})=t$, and likewise fix $y,h$ in the other direction. The localization uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-universal-property] gives the claimed inverse transition maps. This also specifies the symmetric overlap description.

source.place: Tag 01M4 (lemma-standard-open); agent calculation of both outer overlap maps

proof.text: The extended ideal of the blowup centre on each affine chart is generated by the images of $x,a,y$, by [lem-pc-ideal-sheaf-comap-affine-extension], applied to the closed immersion $V(I)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}A$ and the chart lying above that affine base. In $C_x$ these are $x,xt,x^{n-1}t^n$, generating $(x)$ because $n\ge2$. In $C_a$ they are $ar,a,as$, generating $(a)$. In $C_y$ they generate $(y)$ symmetrically. By [def-nagata-extended-ideal] the closed inverse image of the centre is precisely the subscheme cut out by this ideal. Quotienting gives $C_x/(x)=\overline R[t]$, $C_y/(y)=\overline R[h]$ and $C_a/(a)=\overline R[r,s]/(rs-\epsilon)$. These isomorphisms send coefficients to their classes and the displayed variables to themselves; their inverse maps are defined on those generators, and each defining relation becomes zero. Here $a^{n-2}$ reduces to $1$ for $n=2$ and to $0$ for $n>2$.

Restrict the transition formulas to these quotient rings. The first--middle overlap has $r=t^{-1}$ and $s=\epsilon t$; the third--middle one has $s=h^{-1}$ and $r=\epsilon h$. For example $s=x^{n-2}t^{n-1}$ modulo $x$ is $t$ when $n=2$ and $0$ otherwise, and the other formula is symmetric. For $n=2$ the relation $rs=1$ makes both $r,s$ units in the middle quotient. Hence the entire middle chart is each adjacent overlap and, in the first chart, the outer--outer overlap $D(t^2)=D(t)$; there $h=t/t^2=t^{-1}$. For $n>2$ the element $q=x^{n-2}t^n$ becomes $0$ modulo $x$, so the outer--outer overlap is empty. The adjacent overlaps remain $D(r)$ on the branch $s=0$ and $D(s)$ on the branch $r=0$. These conclusions use prime ideals to interpret $D(0)=\varnothing$ and $D(t^2)=D(t)$, so also hold over the possibly nonreduced ring $\overline R$; when $a$ is a unit all three quotient schemes are empty.
